1.meaning: An interrogative meaning 'About what?' — it is the question-word 'what' fused with the preposition 'about/concerning'. The phrase opens the surah by asking what subject people are questioning one another over. Note the question-word's final letter has been dropped for emphasis and ease of speech.
1.grammar: This is the preposition ʿan ('about') joined to the interrogative mā ('what'). When 'what' follows a preposition in a question, its long vowel is shortened and the final alif is dropped, so ʿan + mā contracts to ʿamma. The doubled 'm' (shown by the shadda) is where the 'n' of ʿan has merged into the 'm' of mā. So the whole word literally asks 'about what?' and serves as the object of the asking in the next word.
1.root: — (built from the particle ʿan + the interrogative mā; no triliteral root)

2.meaning: 'They are asking one another' / 'they keep questioning each other' — a present-tense verb describing a back-and-forth, mutual questioning among a group. The form carries the sense of people repeatedly putting the question to one another.

parts.en: ask / question (Form VI stem from س-ء-ل)

2.grammar: A present/imperfect verb in Form VI, the pattern that expresses people doing something to one another (reciprocal action) — here, mutually questioning. The opening ya- marks third person and the -ta- infix marks the Form VI reciprocal sense. The stem sāʾal- carries all three root consonants: the hamza (ء) and the lām (ل) are the second and third radicals of س-ء-ل, not part of the ending. The final -ūna marks 'they' (masculine plural) with the verb in its indicative state (an ongoing, unfinished action: 'are asking'). Putting it together gives ya-ta-sāʾal-ūna = yatasāʾalūna, with the short 'a' kept between the hamza and the lām.
2.root: س-ء-ل (s-ʾ-l) — to ask, to question, to request

1.meaning: The preposition 'about / concerning'. It points to the topic of the questioning: they are asking about something. Here it introduces the thing being asked about ('about the news').
1.grammar: This is the fixed preposition ʿan ('about'). Its final letter normally carries no vowel, but here it is given a helping '-i' (ʿani) purely to smooth pronunciation into the following word that begins with 'the' (al-). The '-i' is not a case ending; it only prevents two unvowelled letters from colliding. A preposition like this puts the noun after it into the genitive (the 'of/about' case).

2.meaning: 'The news / the tiding / the announcement' — and in context, the momentous Report: the news of the Resurrection and the Hereafter that people dispute. It denotes weighty, significant information that is conveyed.
2.grammar: A noun, 'the news', made definite by al- ('the'). The final '-i' (kasra) is the genitive case ending: it appears because the noun follows the preposition ʿan ('about'), so it reads 'about THE news'. The 'l' of al- is fully pronounced here (al-naba-i) since 'n' is one of the letters that does not absorb the article's 'l' in this written form. The ending '-i' signals the word is governed by the preceding preposition.

3.meaning: 'The great / the tremendous / the momentous' — an adjective stressing immense magnitude and gravity. Describing the news, it conveys that this is no ordinary report but one of overwhelming importance.
3.grammar: An adjective, 'the great', describing 'the news' (l-naba-i) in the previous word. Adjectives in Arabic match the noun they describe, so because 'the news' is definite and in the genitive ('-i') case, this adjective likewise takes al- ('the') and the genitive '-i' ending. The matching '-i' ending shows it belongs to the same phrase: 'the GREAT news'. The īm vowel pattern (ʿaẓīm) is the standard shape for this kind of intensive descriptive adjective.
3.root: ع-ظ-م (ʿ-ẓ-m) — greatness, magnitude, tremendousness

1.meaning: 'Which / that' — the masculine singular relative pronoun. It links back to 'the great news' and introduces a description of it: '...the news ABOUT WHICH they differ.' It functions like English 'which/that' opening a relative clause.
1.grammar: A relative pronoun meaning 'which/that', referring to a single masculine thing — here 'the (great) news'. It is a fixed, unchanging word (it does not take case endings), so its form stays the same regardless of its role in the sentence. It sets up the clause that follows ('over which they disagree'), telling us more about the news just mentioned.

2.meaning: 'They' — the detached/standalone pronoun for a group of males (or a mixed group). It is used as a separate word for emphasis, here highlighting the subject of the verb: 'they (it is they who) differ over it.'
2.grammar: An independent subject pronoun, 'they' (masculine plural). Unlike pronouns that attach to the end of a word, this one stands alone and typically begins or emphasizes the subject of a sentence. It is invariable — it has no case ending and never changes shape. Here it is the subject: 'they ... are in disagreement.'

3.meaning: 'Concerning it / about it / in it' — the preposition 'in/about/concerning' with an attached 'it', referring back to the news. It marks the matter over which the dispute occurs: it is concerning THIS that they differ.
3.grammar: The preposition fī ('in/about/concerning') with the attached pronoun 'it/him' joined to its end. Because the pronoun follows a preposition, it appears in its object form, and its vowel shifts to '-hi' (rather than '-hu') in harmony with the long 'ī' just before it. Together it means 'about it', pointing to the news as the subject of the disagreement.
3.root: — (a preposition + attached pronoun; no triliteral root)

4.meaning: 'Ones who differ / those in disagreement' — an active descriptive noun (a 'doer' word) for people who hold conflicting views, who are at variance with one another. In context: regarding the news, they are people split into differing opinions (some believing, some denying).

parts.en: they / ones who (masc. plural, subject form)

4.grammar: An active participle — a noun-like word naming the doers of an action, here 'ones who differ' — built on Form VIII, the pattern that often conveys doing something among/to oneself (mutual or self-involved action), fitting 'differing with one another'. The mu- prefix marks 'the one who does X'. The '-ūna' ending makes it masculine plural ('those who...') and marks it as the predicate/subject in the nominative (the 'doer' case), completing 'they are ones who differ.'
4.root: خ-ل-ف (kh-l-f) — to differ, to be at variance, to succeed/come after

1.meaning: A sharp word of rebuke and restraint — 'No indeed! / Nay! / Stop right there!' It checks and rejects the disputers' attitude, cutting off their doubt before the warning that follows. It is not a plain 'no' to a question but a deterrent: 'By no means — let them desist.'

parts.en: no indeed! / nay! / by no means!

1.grammar: A fixed exclamatory particle of rebuke and deterrence. It takes no endings and never changes. Its job is rhetorical: to halt the wrong notion just expressed (their disputing) and brace the listener for the correction and warning that comes next ('they will soon know'). Read it as a firm, emphatic 'No!'

2.meaning: 'They will soon know / they are going to find out' — a present-tense 'to know' verb pushed into the near future, used as a veiled threat: the deniers will shortly come to realize the truth they now dispute. The attached future-marker stresses that this realization is imminent and certain.
2.grammar: A present/imperfect verb 'to know', turned into the near future by the prefixed sa- ('soon/shall'). The ya- marks third person and the '-ūna' ending marks 'they' (masculine plural) in the verb's normal indicative state (a real, expected future event). The tone is admonitory — 'they will certainly, and soon, find out.'

1.meaning: 'Then / thereafter / again' — a connecting word linking statements in sequence, with a sense of 'and furthermore' or 'yet again'. Here it adds a second, reinforcing warning after the first, implying an ordered, weightier follow-up.
1.grammar: A fixed connecting particle (conjunction) meaning 'then/thereafter'. It joins two clauses in succession and, unlike a simple 'and', suggests a gap, a ranking, or an added emphasis between them. It takes no endings and never changes form. Here it ties the repeated warning to the first: 'then, again, they will know.'

2.meaning: A sharp word of rebuke and restraint — 'No indeed! / Nay! / Stop right there!' It checks and rejects the disputers' attitude, cutting off their doubt before the warning that follows. It is not a plain 'no' to a question but a deterrent: 'By no means — let them desist.'

parts.en: no indeed! / nay! / by no means!

2.grammar: A fixed exclamatory particle of rebuke and deterrence. It takes no endings and never changes. Its job is rhetorical: to halt the wrong notion just expressed (their disputing) and brace the listener for the correction and warning that comes next ('they will soon know'). Read it as a firm, emphatic 'No!'

3.meaning: 'They will soon know / they are going to find out' — a present-tense 'to know' verb pushed into the near future, used as a veiled threat: the deniers will shortly come to realize the truth they now dispute. The attached future-marker stresses that this realization is imminent and certain.
3.grammar: A present/imperfect verb 'to know', turned into the near future by the prefixed sa- ('soon/shall'). The ya- marks third person and the '-ūna' ending marks 'they' (masculine plural) in the verb's normal indicative state (a real, expected future event). The tone is admonitory — 'they will certainly, and soon, find out.'
3.root: ع-ل-م (ʿ-l-m) — to know, knowledge, awareness

1.meaning: An opening particle meaning 'Did … not?' or 'Have … not?'. It is made of the question-word 'a' ('did/have?') fused with the negation 'lam' ('not'). Together they pose a rhetorical question that expects the answer 'yes' — i.e. 'Surely We did…' — drawing the listener to affirm what follows.
1.grammar: Two particles joined. The 'a-' at the front turns the phrase into a question; 'lam' is a negator that pushes the following present-tense verb back into past meaning ('did not…'). Combined as a rhetorical question, it amounts to a strong affirmation ('Have We not indeed…?'). 'lam' also forces the verb after it into the jussive mood, which is why the next verb drops its final vowel.

2.meaning: 'We make / We set / We place.' Here it carries the sense of appointing or rendering something into a particular state — to make the earth into a resting-place. Because it follows 'lam', its meaning shifts to the past: 'We did (not) make.'

parts.en: helping vowel (kasra) added to ease pronunciation before the next word

2.grammar: A present-tense verb with the 'na-' prefix meaning 'we' (the royal/majestic 'We' of Allah). Governed by the preceding 'lam', it is in the jussive mood, so its base ending is a silent stop (sukūn) — 'najʿal'. The final '-i' you hear is not a case ending; it is an extra helping vowel slipped in to avoid two unvowelled consonants meeting the following word 'al-arḍa'.
2.root: ج-ع-ل (j-ʿ-l) — to make, to render, to appoint

3.meaning: 'The earth' — the ground, the land, the world beneath us.
3.grammar: A definite noun ('the earth') carrying the accusative ending '-a'. The '-a' marks it as the direct object of the verb 'najʿal' — it is the thing being made into a resting-place: 'We made the earth (a bed).'
3.root: أ-ر-ض (ʾ-r-ḍ) — earth, land

4.meaning: 'A bed / a cradle / a smoothed-out resting place.' The word pictures the earth spread flat and made comfortable, like bedding prepared for someone to lie on or a cradle that holds and steadies its occupant.

parts.en: accusative ending with 'nunation' (-an): marks an indefinite object

4.grammar: An indefinite noun in the accusative case. The '-an' ending (accusative + nunation, the 'n' sound marking indefiniteness, 'a bed') shows it is the second object of 'jaʿala' (to make X into Y): 'made the earth INTO a resting-place.'
4.root: م-ه-د (m-h-d) — to spread out, smooth, prepare (a bed/cradle)

1.meaning: 'And the mountains.' The connecting 'and' links this to the previous statement, continuing the list of Allah's acts; 'the mountains' are the great elevations fixed in the earth.

parts.en: 'and' (connective; doubled in sound after the preceding word)

1.grammar: 'wa' is the connective 'and'. The noun 'the mountains' takes the accusative ending '-a' because it is the object of an understood/continued verb 'made' — 'and (We made) the mountains (as pegs).' 'jibāl' is a broken plural (jamʿ taksīr) of 'jabal', formed by reshaping the word's internal vowel pattern rather than by adding a suffix. Broken plurals are treated grammatically like a singular feminine noun, so it simply takes the ordinary single '-a' to mark it as the object.

2.meaning: '(As) pegs / stakes / tent-pins.' The image is of mountains driven into the earth like the pegs that hold a tent firm, stabilizing the ground.

parts.en: accusative ending with nunation (-an): indefinite object

2.grammar: An indefinite noun in the accusative case, '-an' (accusative + nunation, 'pegs'). It is the second object of the verb 'to make' — 'made the mountains (as) pegs' — describing what the mountains were appointed to be.
2.root: و-ت-د (w-t-d) — to fix firmly; peg, stake

1.meaning: 'And We created you.' It joins a new act to the list and states that Allah brought the addressed people into existence.
1.grammar: A past-tense verb. The suffix '-nā' on the end means 'we' (the doers — the majestic 'We' of Allah); the further suffix '-kum' means 'you all' (the ones acted upon). So the single word says 'We created you (plural).' Because it is genuinely past tense, the verb form is fixed and shows no case ending.
1.root: خ-ل-ق (kh-l-q) — to create, originate, bring into being

2.meaning: '(In) pairs / as mates / kinds' — male and female, paired and matched. It describes humankind as created in complementary couples.

parts.en: pairs, mates, spouses, kinds (plural of zawj)

2.grammar: An indefinite noun in the accusative case, '-an' (accusative + nunation, 'pairs'). Here it functions as a descriptive complement (a 'state') of the object 'you' — telling how you were created: 'created you (being) pairs / in pairs.'

1.meaning: 'And We made / appointed / set.' It continues the series of divine acts; 'jaʿala' here means to render something into a given purpose or state.
1.grammar: A past-tense verb with the attached '-nā' meaning 'we' (the majestic 'We' of Allah) as the subject: 'We made.' As a past-tense form it is grammatically fixed and carries no case ending. The verb 'jaʿala' typically takes two objects (make X into Y), set up by what follows.

2.meaning: 'Your sleep' — the rest/slumber belonging to the people addressed.
2.grammar: A noun, 'sleep', with the attached pronoun '-kum' ('your', plural) showing possession. It carries the accusative ending '-a' because it is the first object of 'jaʿalnā' — the thing being made into something: 'made your sleep (a means of rest).'

3.meaning: '(As) a means of rest / repose / a cessation.' The word suggests cutting off activity so the body is stilled and restored — sleep as a pause that renews.

parts.en: accusative ending with nunation (-an): indefinite object

3.grammar: An indefinite noun in the accusative case, '-an' (accusative + nunation, 'a rest'). It is the second object of 'jaʿala' (make X into Y): 'made your sleep (into) a means of rest.'
3.root: س-ب-ت (s-b-t) — to rest, cease, be still

1.meaning: 'And We made / appointed / set.' It continues the series of divine acts; 'jaʿala' here means to render something into a given purpose or state.
1.grammar: A past-tense verb with the attached '-nā' meaning 'we' (the majestic 'We' of Allah) as the subject: 'We made.' As a past-tense form it is grammatically fixed and carries no case ending. The verb 'jaʿala' typically takes two objects (make X into Y), set up by what follows.

2.meaning: 'The night' — the dark portion of the day, the time of cover and stillness.

parts.en: 'the' (definite article; its 'l' assimilates into the following 'l' sound)

2.grammar: A definite noun ('the night') in the accusative case. The '-a' ending marks it as the object of the continued verb 'made' — 'and (We made) the night (as a covering).' Note the article's 'l' merges into the word's own 'l' (al-layl, pronounced 'allayl'), a regular sound rule.

3.meaning: A covering or garment; here the night is likened to a garment that wraps and conceals, drawing a veil of darkness over everything so people can rest.
3.grammar: An indefinite masculine noun. The final -an (tanwīn fatḥa) marks the accusative case: it is the object/complement of the verb 'made' — 'and made the night [as] a covering.' The doubled-n sound (nunation) signals that the noun is indefinite ('a covering,' not 'the covering').
3.root: ل-ب-س (l-b-s) — to wear, clothe, cover over

1.meaning: 'And We made / appointed / set.' It continues the series of divine acts; 'jaʿala' here means to render something into a given purpose or state.
1.grammar: A past-tense verb with the attached '-nā' meaning 'we' (the majestic 'We' of Allah) as the subject: 'We made.' As a past-tense form it is grammatically fixed and carries no case ending. The verb 'jaʿala' typically takes two objects (make X into Y), set up by what follows.

2.meaning: The daytime — the bright period of daylight, contrasted with the night.
2.grammar: A definite masculine noun with the article 'al-' ('the'). The l of 'al-' assimilates into the following n (heard as 'an-nahār,' shown by the shadda on the n). The final -a (fatḥa) marks the accusative case: it is the object of the verb 'made' — 'and made the day.'
2.root: ن-ه-ر (n-h-r) — daylight, the flowing brightness of day (also 'to flow')

3.meaning: A time or means of living — the active part of life when people seek their sustenance and earn their living; the day is appointed as the season for labor and provision.
3.grammar: An indefinite noun of place/time formed on the pattern mafʿāl. The mīm at the front is the derivational prefix that turns a root into a noun of place or time, and the long ā after the second root-letter appears because the middle root-letter is weak (the yāʾ of ʿ-y-sh lengthens into ā rather than showing as a consonant). The final -an (tanwīn fatḥa) marks the accusative: it is the second object/complement of 'made' — 'made the day [for] livelihood.' The nunation marks it as indefinite.
3.root: ع-ي-ش (ʿ-y-sh) — to live, livelihood, means of life

1.meaning: And We built / constructed / raised up as a structure — a verb of building, here said of Allah erecting the heavens like a solid edifice.
1.grammar: A past-tense verb meaning 'built.' The attached -nā at the end means 'we' (the royal 'We' of divine majesty): 'We built.' The opening wa- means 'and'; its w is doubled in pronunciation (shown by the shadda) because it links smoothly to the preceding word. There is no case ending here — this is a verb, and -nā is its subject.
1.root: ب-ن-ي (b-n-y) — to build, construct, erect a structure

2.meaning: Above you / over you — directly overhead, in the space above the addressees.

parts.en: accusative ending (here marking an adverb of place)

2.grammar: A place-word ('above') functioning as an adverb of location. The -a ending (fatḥa) is the accusative, the normal case for such adverbs of place — 'in the place above.' The attached -kum means 'you' (masculine plural, addressing many people): together 'above you all.'
2.root: ف-و-ق (f-w-q) — to be above, to surpass, height/over

3.meaning: Seven — the cardinal number seven, here counting the heavens.
3.grammar: An indefinite number-noun ('seven'). The final -an (tanwīn fatḥa) marks the accusative case: it is the object of 'We built' — 'We built seven [heavens] above you.' The counted noun (heavens) is left unstated but understood. The nunation shows it is indefinite.
3.root: س-ب-ع (s-b-ʿ) — seven (the number)

4.meaning: Strong, firm, sturdy — solidly built and unshakable; describing the seven heavens as mighty, well-fortified structures.
4.grammar: An indefinite adjective in its broken (internal) plural form — 'strong/firm ones' — describing the plural 'seven [heavens].' The final -an (tanwīn fatḥa) marks the accusative, agreeing with the noun it describes ('seven... strong ones'). The plural shape (pattern fiʿāl) matches the plurality of the heavens being described.
4.root: ش-د-د (sh-d-d) — to be strong, firm, intense, severe

1.meaning: 'And We made / appointed / set.' It continues the series of divine acts; 'jaʿala' here means to render something into a given purpose or state.
1.grammar: A past-tense verb with the attached '-nā' meaning 'we' (the majestic 'We' of Allah) as the subject: 'We made.' As a past-tense form it is grammatically fixed and carries no case ending. The verb 'jaʿala' typically takes two objects (make X into Y), set up by what follows.

2.meaning: A lamp — a bright light-giving source; here it refers to the sun, pictured as a blazing lamp set in the sky.
2.grammar: An indefinite masculine noun. The final -an (tanwīn fatḥa) marks the accusative case: it is the object of the (understood) verb 'placed/made' — 'and placed a lamp.' The nunation marks it as indefinite ('a lamp').

3.meaning: Blazing, intensely burning, radiating great heat and light — an emphatic description of the lamp (the sun) as fiercely luminous.
3.grammar: An indefinite adjective on the intensive pattern faʿʿāl (the doubled middle letter, shown by the shadda, conveys an intense, continuous quality — 'fiercely blazing'). The whole word is wahhāj; the wāw here is the first root-letter, not a separate 'and.' In the written text the shadda on that wāw comes from the -an ending of the preceding sirājan merging into it (assimilation), not from any prefix. It describes 'a lamp,' so its final -an (tanwīn fatḥa) is accusative, agreeing with sirājan.
3.root: و-ه-ج (w-h-j) — to blaze, glow, burn with heat and light

1.meaning: And We sent down / caused to descend — a verb of bringing something down from above, here said of Allah sending rain down from the clouds.

parts.en: sent down, caused to descend (past stem)

1.grammar: A past-tense verb in the causative (form IV) pattern 'anzala — 'to send/bring down.' The attached -nā means 'we' (the divine 'We'): 'We sent down.' The opening wa- means 'and' (its w doubled in pronunciation joining the previous word). Being a verb, it has no case ending; -nā is its subject.
1.root: ن-ز-ل (n-z-l) — to descend, come down; (form IV) to send down

2.meaning: From / out of — a particle marking the starting point or source from which something comes.
2.grammar: A preposition meaning 'from,' marking origin or source. Its base form is 'min'; the final vowel here is -a ('mina') simply to ease pronunciation before the following word that begins with the article 'al-' (a connecting vowel, not a case ending — particles do not take cases). It puts the next noun into the genitive: 'from the rainclouds.'

3.meaning: The rain-laden clouds — clouds heavy and ripe with moisture, on the verge of pouring out rain; the source from which the water is sent down.
3.grammar: A definite feminine plural noun with the article 'al-' ('the'). It is an active participle (form IV, muf'il pattern) meaning 'the ones producing/squeezing out rain' — i.e. rain-laden clouds. The -āt is the sound feminine plural ('-s'). The final -i (kasra) is the genitive case, required because it follows the preposition 'from' (mina): 'from the rainclouds.'
3.root: ع-ص-ر (ʿ-ṣ-r) — to squeeze, press out; (of clouds) to be wrung out as rain

4.meaning: Water — here specifically rain-water sent down from the clouds. The indefinite, unbounded sense ('water', 'some water') fits its role as the life-giving substance Allah pours down.
4.grammar: A masculine noun in the accusative case. The '-an' ending (written with tanwīn / nunation) does two things: the final '-a' marks it as the direct object of the verb 'sent down' (He sent down water), and the doubled 'n' sound marks it as indefinite ('water', not 'the water'). The hamza belongs to the root, so the noun is mā'an.

5.meaning: Pouring out abundantly, gushing torrentially. An intensive description of the rain-water: not a trickle but a heavy, copious downpour.
5.grammar: An intensive adjective on the faʿʿāl pattern (doubled middle root letter), which conveys 'doing the action much/abundantly' — hence 'pouring in torrents'. It describes the noun 'water' (id 36), so it copies that noun's case: the '-an' ending is indefinite accusative, matching mā'an. The doubled 'j' (shadda) is the intensive pattern, not an ending.
5.root: ث-ج-ج (th-j-j) — to pour out, gush forth

1.meaning: So that We may bring forth / produce. Expresses Allah's purpose in sending the rain: in order to bring out grain and plants from the earth.

parts.en: bring forth / cause to come out (Form IV verb stem)

1.grammar: A present-tense verb, 'first person plural' (We), built on the causative Form IV (ʾakhraja = 'to bring out'), so it means 'we cause to come out / bring forth'. The 'nu-' prefix marks the 'we' subject. The 'li-' particle at the front means 'so that' and puts the verb into the subjunctive mood, which is why the ending is '-a' (linukhrija) rather than the usual '-u'; this '-a' signals purpose ('in order that We bring forth').
1.root: خ-ر-ج (kh-r-j) — to go out, come forth

2.meaning: By it / by means of it / thereby — i.e. by means of that water. The pronoun 'it' refers back to the water that was sent down.
2.grammar: A preposition 'bi-' ('with, by means of') joined to the attached pronoun '-hi' ('it'). Anything following the preposition 'bi-' takes the genitive form, which is why the pronoun appears as '-hi' (with an 'i' vowel) rather than '-hu'. In the standard Hafs ʿan ʿĀṣim reading recited here, it is pronounced bihi with a short kasra (the pronoun is not lengthened, because the preceding letter is vowelless); the long-vowel pronunciation bihī belongs to other recitation traditions. Together: 'by means of it'.

3.meaning: Grain — seeds/cereals such as wheat and barley; the edible grain that grows from the watered earth. Indefinite: 'grain', taken collectively.
3.grammar: A masculine collective noun in the accusative case. The '-an' ending marks it as indefinite ('grain' in general) and as the direct object of the verb 'bring forth' (id 38) — 'that We may bring forth grain'. The doubled 'b' (shadda) is part of the root (ḥ-b-b), not an ending.
3.root: ح-ب-ب (ḥ-b-b) — grain, seed; (also love)

4.meaning: And vegetation / plant growth — green plants and herbage. Paired with 'grain' as a second thing brought forth by the rain.
4.grammar: The conjunction 'wa-' ('and') plus the noun 'vegetation'. Because it is joined by 'and' to the earlier object 'grain' (id 40), it shares the same role and ending: the '-an' is indefinite accusative, marking it as another direct object of 'bring forth' ('grain and vegetation'). (The doubled 'w' shown in the script is a recitation assimilation with the preceding word, not part of the noun.)

1.meaning: And gardens / orchards — lush enclosed groves of trees. Plural, here listing a further blessing produced by the rain.
1.grammar: The conjunction 'wa-' ('and') plus 'gardens', the sound feminine plural of jannah ('garden'). Sound feminine plurals use the same ending for both the object case and the genitive case, and that ending is '-in' (here indefinite, with tanwīn) rather than '-an'; so even as a further object of 'bring forth' it correctly reads jannātin. The long 'ā' (jannāt) is the plural marker. The doubled 'n' is part of the root.
1.root: ج-ن-ن (j-n-n) — to cover, conceal; (a garden 'covers' its ground with foliage)

2.meaning: Dense / luxuriantly intertwined — describing gardens whose trees and branches are thickly tangled together with rich foliage.
2.grammar: A plural form, alfāf, describing the gardens as densely tangled and leafy. The opening 'a-' is part of the word itself, not the definite article 'al-'. It functions as a ḥāl (a circumstantial complement — 'the gardens being densely intertwined'), which is why it takes the accusative '-an' (alfāfan): a ḥāl is always in the accusative regardless of its referent's case. Note it does NOT simply copy the case of 'gardens' (id 42); a plain attributive adjective for jannātin would have ended in '-in', so the '-an' here specifically signals the ḥāl/adverbial-accusative role.
2.root: ل-ف-ف (l-f-f) — to wrap, fold, wind together

1.meaning: A particle of emphasis placed at the start of a sentence to assert what follows strongly and certainly — roughly 'Indeed…', 'Truly…', 'It is certainly the case that…'. It has no single English word; it stresses the truth of the whole statement.
1.grammar: An emphatic particle that opens a sentence. It puts the noun right after it (here 'the Day of Decision') into the accusative form, and gives the sense 'Indeed/Truly…'. The doubled 'n' (shadda) is intrinsic to the particle; it has no case ending of its own.

2.meaning: The Day — here the great appointed Day, identified in the next word as the Day of Decision/Judgment.
2.grammar: A masculine noun, 'day'. The '-a' ending is accusative; it appears because this noun is the subject that the emphatic particle 'inna' (id 44) governs — 'inna' forces the following noun into this '-a' form. It is also the first part of the phrase 'the Day OF Decision', completed by the next word.

3.meaning: The Decision / the Judgment / the sorting-out — the Day when Allah will definitively separate truth from falsehood and judge between all creatures. 'al-faṣl' is the decisive distinguishing/verdict.
3.grammar: The definite article 'al-' ('the') plus the noun 'decision/separation'. The '-i' ending is genitive: it links this word to the one before it in a possessive 'X of Y' chain — 'the Day OF the Decision'. So yawma l-faṣli = 'the Day of the Decision/Judgment'.
3.root: ف-ص-ل (f-ṣ-l) — to separate, distinguish, decide between

4.meaning: Was / has come to be — the verb 'to be' in the past tense. In a context like this it states an established, settled fact ('it is / has ever been'), here that the Day of Decision is a fixed appointed time.
4.grammar: A past-tense verb meaning 'was / has been', in the third person masculine singular ('he/it'). The final '-a' (kāna) is the standard ending marking a 'he/it' subject in the past tense — here the subject is 'it' (the Day). Though past in form, kāna often expresses a fixed, ongoing reality, so it renders naturally as 'is' an appointed time.
4.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — to be, to exist, to come to be

5.meaning: An appointed time, a fixed and pre-determined moment set in advance — a deadline or rendezvous point on the timeline of creation. Here it names the Day of Decision as something Allah has precisely scheduled.
5.grammar: A noun in the indefinite accusative. The doubled final '-an' (tanwīn) marks it as indefinite ('an appointed time') and the accusative case here is because it is the predicate of the preceding 'kāna'-type statement ('the Day is an appointed time'). The pattern 'mī-' on this root signals a noun denoting the time or instrument of an action.
5.root: و-ق-ت (w-q-t) — time, the fixing of an appointed moment

1.meaning: The Day — a specific day; here the Day of Resurrection, presented as the appointed moment on which the events that follow take place.
1.grammar: A noun ending in '-a' (accusative). The '-a' here functions adverbially — 'on the Day…' — anchoring the following clause in time (it stands as an adverb of time / or in apposition to the preceding 'appointed time'). The bare '-a' without tanwīn reflects that it is bound to the clause that follows it ('the Day [on which]…').
1.root: ي-و-م (y-w-m) — day, a span of time

2.meaning: It is blown / a blowing is made into — the act of sounding a blast, as breath is driven through the Trumpet. Stated impersonally: 'there is a blowing,' without naming who blows.
2.grammar: A present-tense passive verb, 3rd person masculine singular. The prefix 'yu-' with the internal vowelling (u–a) makes it passive: 'is blown' rather than 'blows.' The final '-u' is the indicative ending, marking a plain, ongoing/future statement of fact. Being passive, the doer is left unnamed; the thing blown ('in the Trumpet') follows.

3.meaning: In / into — a preposition placing something inside or within. Here it marks where the blowing is directed: into the Trumpet.
3.grammar: An indeclinable preposition; its form never changes. It governs the noun after it, putting that noun in the genitive case (hence 'the Trumpet' takes the '-i' ending that follows).

4.meaning: The Trumpet — the great horn whose blast signals the Resurrection and the gathering of all creatures.
4.grammar: A definite noun ('the Trumpet'). The '-i' ending is genitive: it is required because the noun is governed by the preceding preposition 'fī' ('in the Trumpet'). The 'al-' assimilates into the following 'ṣ' (a 'sun letter'), so it is pronounced 'aṣ-ṣūr'.
4.root: ص-و-ر (ṣ-w-r) — here the sounding-horn/trumpet (distinct from the homographic root for 'forming/shaping')

5.meaning: So you come / you will come forth — you (a group) advance and present yourselves, arriving on the scene. The opening 'fa-' shows this follows as the immediate result of the blast.

parts.en: you come (2nd person prefix + root stem)

5.grammar: A present-tense verb, 2nd person masculine plural ('you all come/will come'). The 'ta-' prefix marks 'you,' and the '-ūna' ending marks a masculine plural subject in the indicative (a plain statement); its long 'ū' belongs entirely to this suffix, not to the stem. The stem itself is 'taʾt-' (prefix ta- plus the root radicals ʾ-t from ʾ-t-y, the final weak 'y' dropping before the plural ending). The prefixed 'fa-' means 'and so / then,' linking this as the consequence of the Trumpet being blown.

6.meaning: In crowds / in throngs — group upon group, troops of people coming in successive multitudes rather than one by one.
6.grammar: A noun in the indefinite accusative plural. 'Afwāj' is a 'broken' (internal) plural of 'fawj' (a troop/band). The '-an' ending (tanwīn) marks it indefinite, and the accusative case functions adverbially here — describing the manner of coming: 'you come (in the state of being) crowds.'
6.root: ف-و-ج (f-w-j) — a troop, band, or crowd moving together

1.meaning: And it is opened / thrown open — and (the sky) is laid wide open. The act is done to it (passive): it is caused to open up.
1.grammar: A past-tense passive verb, 3rd person feminine singular: 'is/was opened' (done to it, not by it). The internal vowels (u–i) make it passive, and the suffix '-at' marks a feminine subject — agreeing with 'the sky,' which is grammatically feminine. The final '-i' is a helping vowel added to ease pronunciation before the next word (the 't' would otherwise be silent). The prefixed 'wa-' means 'and.' Though past in form, it describes a certain future event.

2.meaning: The sky / the heaven — the visible firmament overarching the earth, which on that Day is torn open.
2.grammar: A definite noun ('the sky'). The '-u' ending is nominative, marking it as the subject — the thing that 'is opened.' The 'al-' assimilates into the following 's' (a 'sun letter'), so it is pronounced 'as-samā'.' This noun is feminine, which is why its verb carries the feminine '-at' ending.
2.root: س-م-و (s-m-w) — height, that which is high above

3.meaning: So it becomes / and it comes to be — and (the sky) turns into something: as a result of being opened, it ends up as gateways. 'Fa-' marks this as the outcome.
3.grammar: The past-tense verb 'to be/become,' 3rd person feminine singular ('it became'). The '-at' ending marks the feminine subject (the sky). 'Kāna' here means 'became / came to be,' and it puts its complement ('gateways') into the accusative case. The prefixed 'fa-' means 'and so,' presenting this as the result. Past in form, it refers to a future certainty.
3.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — being, coming into existence

4.meaning: Gateways / gates — wide openings or doorways; the torn-open sky becomes full of gaping passages, as if it were all doors.
4.grammar: A noun in the indefinite accusative plural. 'Abwāb' is a 'broken' (internal) plural of 'bāb' (a door/gate). The '-an' ending (tanwīn) marks it indefinite, and the accusative case is because it is the complement of 'became' ('it became gateways').
4.root: ب-و-ب (b-w-b) — a door, gate, or opening

1.meaning: And they are set moving / made to move along — and (the mountains) are driven and carried off, set in motion until they pass away like a mirage. The doubled middle letter stresses an intense, thorough moving.

parts.en: was/is made to move (intensive passive stem)

1.grammar: A past-tense passive verb, 3rd person feminine singular, of the intensive (doubled-middle) pattern: 'is made to move / is set in motion' (done to them). The internal vowels (u–i) make it passive; the doubled 'y' intensifies the action; and the '-at' suffix marks a feminine singular subject. Although 'the mountains' is plural in meaning, it is an inanimate (non-rational) broken plural, and by the standard rule of Arabic grammar such plurals take feminine singular verb agreement. The final '-i' is a helping vowel before the next word. The prefixed 'wa-' means 'and.' Past in form, it describes a future event.

2.meaning: The mountains — the great rocky masses fixed in the earth. In context (78:20), these seemingly immovable mountains are set in motion and shattered on the Day of Resurrection.
2.grammar: A definite plural noun. 'al-' makes it 'the mountains.' The final -u ending marks it as the subject (the doer/topic) of the sentence — here, the mountains are what gets blown away. (Jīm is a 'moon letter,' so the lām of 'al-' is fully pronounced: al-jibāl.)
2.root: ج-ب-ل (j-b-l) — mountain, to be firmly fixed

3.meaning: So it becomes / and it comes to be — and (the sky) turns into something: as a result of being opened, it ends up as gateways. 'Fa-' marks this as the outcome.
3.grammar: The past-tense verb 'to be/become,' 3rd person feminine singular ('it became'). The '-at' ending marks the feminine subject (the sky). 'Kāna' here means 'became / came to be,' and it puts its complement ('gateways') into the accusative case. The prefixed 'fa-' means 'and so,' presenting this as the result. Past in form, it refers to a future certainty.
3.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — being, coming into existence

4.meaning: A mirage — the shimmering illusion of water seen over hot desert sand that vanishes on approach. The shattered mountains become as insubstantial as this empty appearance.
4.grammar: An indefinite noun. The final -an (tanwīn, the doubled 'n' sound) marks both indefiniteness ('a mirage') and the accusative case here functioning as the predicate after 'become' — what the mountains turn into.
4.root: س-ر-ب (s-r-b) — to flow/run; mirage that seems to flow

1.meaning: A particle of emphasis placed at the start of a sentence to assert what follows strongly and certainly — roughly 'Indeed…', 'Truly…', 'It is certainly the case that…'. It has no single English word; it stresses the truth of the whole statement.
1.grammar: An emphatic particle that opens a sentence. It puts the noun right after it (here 'the Day of Decision') into the accusative form, and gives the sense 'Indeed/Truly…'. The doubled 'n' (shadda) is intrinsic to the particle; it has no case ending of its own.

2.meaning: Hell (Jahannam) — the proper name of the abode of punishment in the Hereafter. More than a generic 'hell,' it is a specific named place described throughout the Qur'an as a destination for the wrongdoers.
2.grammar: A proper name serving as the subject (ism) of the verb 'kānat' — a nominative position, where a regular noun would take -u. It takes a single -a ending because, as a foreign-origin proper name, it is 'diptote': it never takes tanwīn, and it uses -a in place of both the nominative -u and the genitive -i.

3.meaning: It was / it is — a verb of being from 'kāna.' It establishes a state of being for its subject (here, Hell); in such contexts the past-tense form expresses a settled, enduring reality ('Hell has ever been / is').
3.grammar: Past-tense verb 'to be.' The -at ending means the subject is feminine singular ('she/it'), agreeing with Jahannam (treated as feminine). 'Kāna' links its subject to a following description (the predicate 'lying in wait'), which then takes the accusative.
3.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — being, to be/become

4.meaning: A place of ambush / lying in wait — a lookout post where one watches to waylay those who pass. Hell is portrayed as poised, watching for the wrongdoers as a hunter waits in ambush.
4.grammar: An indefinite noun of place (the 'mi-' pattern often names a place or instrument). The final -an marks indefiniteness and the accusative case, because it is the predicate (the description) completing 'Hell is/has been...'.
4.root: ر-ص-د (r-ṣ-d) — to watch, lie in wait, observe

1.meaning: For the transgressors — those who exceed all bounds in rebellion and oppression (from ṭughyān, overflowing arrogance against Allah). The combined sense is 'belonging to / destined for the boundary-overstepping rebels.'
1.grammar: Preposition 'li-' ('for') joined to a definite plural active participle. The 'a' of 'al-' drops after 'li-' and the lām doubles in sound (li-ṭ-ṭāghīn). The -īna ending is the masculine plural form used after a preposition: 'for the transgressors.'
1.root: ط-غ-ي (ṭ-gh-y) — to overflow, exceed all limits, tyrannize

2.meaning: A place of return / final resort — the destination one comes back to and settles in. For the transgressors, Hell is the home to which they ultimately return.
2.grammar: An indefinite noun of place ('ma-' pattern: the place where an action happens). The final -an marks indefiniteness and the accusative case — it is a second predicate/complement: Hell is, for them, 'a place of return.'

1.meaning: Remaining / abiding — those who stay and linger in a place for a long, drawn-out time. It describes the wrongdoers as permanent residents of the Fire.
1.grammar: An active participle (the 'one who does X' form) in the masculine plural. The -īna ending here marks the accusative, because it describes the state of the wrongdoers ('remaining therein') — a circumstantial description tied to the previous verse.

2.meaning: In it / therein — the preposition 'in' fused with 'it,' referring back to Hell (feminine). It locates the abiding: they remain inside it.
2.grammar: Preposition 'fī' ('in') with the attached pronoun '-hā' ('it,' feminine), pointing back to Jahannam. Attached pronouns do not change for case; together they mean 'in it / therein.' (The long final vowel is stretched in recitation.)

3.meaning: For ages — successive long stretches of time, one era following another without end. It conveys an immense, unbroken duration of their stay in the Fire.
3.grammar: An indefinite plural noun (the plural of 'ḥuqb,' a long age). The final -an marks indefiniteness and the accusative, here acting as an adverb of time: it tells how long they remain — 'for ages.'
3.root: ح-ق-ب (ḥ-q-b) — a long stretch of time, an age/epoch

1.meaning: Not — a particle of negation. Placed before a present-tense verb, it denies the action: 'they do not / will not...'. Here it negates their tasting of any relief.
1.grammar: A negating particle. It carries no case ending of its own; it simply turns the following present-tense verb negative. With a present-tense verb describing the future, it means 'they will not...'.

2.meaning: They taste — to experience or sample through the sense of taste; by extension, to undergo or feel something directly. Negated by the preceding 'lā,' it means they will get no taste of coolness or drink.
2.grammar: A present-tense verb. The 'ya-' prefix plus the '-ūna' ending together mean 'they (masculine plural) taste.' The -ūna ending is the full indicative form, kept here because no jussive/subjunctive particle shortens it — the negation 'lā' only denies, it does not clip the ending.

3.meaning: In it / therein — the preposition 'in' fused with 'it,' referring back to Hell (feminine). It locates the abiding: they remain inside it.
3.grammar: Preposition 'fī' ('in') with the attached pronoun '-hā' ('it,' feminine), pointing back to Jahannam. Attached pronouns do not change for case; together they mean 'in it / therein.' (The long final vowel is stretched in recitation.)
3.root: — (preposition + pronoun; no triliteral root)

4.meaning: Coolness or cool relief — the refreshing chill of cool air or shade that brings comfort, especially after heat. In context it denotes the cooling respite the inhabitants of Hell will be denied.
4.grammar: A singular masculine noun functioning as the direct object of the verb 'taste'. The final -an (the double-fatha/tanwīn written as ـًا) marks it as indefinite ('a/any coolness') and in the accusative case, which is the case of the thing acted upon — here, what they will not taste.

5.meaning: A linking 'and not' — it joins 'coolness' to the next item ('drink') while extending the negation over it, so the sense is 'neither coolness nor any drink.'
5.grammar: Two particles with no case or tense of their own. 'wa' is the conjunction 'and'; 'lā' is the particle of negation that carries the earlier 'they will not taste' onto the following noun. (The 'w' is written doubled/with shadda because the preceding word's ending assimilates into it in recitation.) Together they mean 'and not …', i.e. 'nor.'

6.meaning: A drink — any beverage or thing one drinks. In context, alongside 'coolness,' it is the second comfort the people of the Fire will not be given.
6.grammar: A singular masculine noun, the second direct object of 'taste' (paired with 'coolness'). The final -an (tanwīn, ـًا) marks it as indefinite ('any drink') and accusative — the case for the object being acted upon, i.e. what they will not taste.

1.meaning: Except / only — a particle of exception that carves out what follows from a preceding negation. After 'they will not taste any coolness or drink,' it introduces the sole grim exception to that statement.
1.grammar: An indeclinable particle of exception (it has no case, tense, or root). It signals that what comes next is excluded from the earlier negation: 'they taste nothing … except ____.' It does not itself change form.

2.meaning: Scalding, boiling water — intensely hot liquid. The form is an adjective ('boiling hot') used as a noun for the searing drink given to the people of the Fire.
2.grammar: A singular masculine noun (originally an intensive adjective on the pattern faʿīl, 'boiling hot'). It stands in the accusative as the thing excepted by 'illā' (matching the earlier accusative objects). The final -an (tanwīn, ـًا) marks it indefinite and accusative: 'except scalding water.'
2.root: ح-م-م (ḥ-m-m) — intense heat, becoming boiling hot

3.meaning: And festering fluid — the dark, foul discharge (pus, oozing matter, or icy-stinking liquid) that runs from the bodies of the punished. Joined by 'and' to 'scalding water' as the second item of the exception.
3.grammar: A conjunction 'wa' ('and') plus a singular masculine noun (intensive pattern faʿʿāl, suggesting something that profusely flows/festers). The noun is accusative, parallel to 'ḥamīm,' as a second item excepted by 'illā.' The final -an (tanwīn, ـًا) marks it indefinite and accusative. (The 'w' is written doubled because the preceding word's ending merges into it in recitation.)
3.root: غ-س-ق (gh-s-q) — to flow/ooze (of a dark, foul fluid); darkness

1.meaning: A recompense — a repayment or requital, the due return given for one's deeds. Here it frames the punishment just described as exactly what their actions earned.
1.grammar: A singular masculine verbal noun in the accusative. The accusative here gives the sense 'as a recompense' (an adverbial/causative accusative explaining why or in what capacity the punishment is given). The final -an (tanwīn, written ـً after the hamza) marks it indefinite and accusative.

2.meaning: Fitting / well-matched — perfectly suited and proportionate. It describes the recompense as exactly corresponding to the deeds: a punishment that matches the crime measure for measure.
2.grammar: A masculine verbal noun on the pattern fiʿāl, used adjectivally to describe the preceding 'recompense'; as its descriptor it shares the accusative case. The final -an (tanwīn, written ـًا with the supporting alif, since the word ends in the consonant qāf) marks it indefinite and accusative, agreeing with 'jazā'an': 'a recompense well-matched.' (The 'w' is written doubled because the preceding word's ending merges into it in recitation.)
2.root: و-ف-ق (w-f-q) — to agree, match, be in accord

1.meaning: Indeed they — an emphatic particle 'inna' ('truly, indeed') used to assert a statement firmly, fused with the attached pronoun 'they.' It introduces the reason for their punishment with certainty: 'It is a fact that they …'
1.grammar: 'inna' is an emphasis particle that strongly affirms the sentence that follows and grammatically governs the noun after it in the accusative. Attached to it is the suffixed pronoun '-hum' ('they'), which serves as its subject. The pronoun ending '-hum' specifically means a group of males (or a mixed group): 'indeed, they …'

2.meaning: They were / they used to — the past-tense of the verb 'to be' for a male group. With a following verb it expresses a sustained or habitual past: 'they used to (keep doing) …'
2.grammar: A past-tense verb. The subject ending '-ū' (the long 'oo', written وا with a silent alif) means the doer is 'they,' a group of three or more males. Paired with the following present-tense verb 'yarjūna,' it shifts the meaning to the continuous/habitual past — 'they used to …' — describing an ongoing attitude during their worldly life.

3.meaning: Not — a particle of negation. Placed before a present-tense verb, it denies the action: 'they do not / will not...'. Here it negates their tasting of any relief.
3.grammar: A negating particle. It carries no case ending of its own; it simply turns the following present-tense verb negative. With a present-tense verb describing the future, it means 'they will not...'.
3.root: — (particle; no root)

4.meaning: Hoping for / expecting — to look forward to something with anticipation (and often with fear of its opposite). In context (negated by the surrounding sense) it means they did NOT anticipate or reckon on facing a reckoning.
4.grammar: A present/ongoing-tense verb. The 'ya-' shape marks 3rd person, and the ending '-ūna' means the subject is 'they' (a group of males) with the action ongoing/repeated. Governed by 'kānū' before it, the pair reads as habitual past: 'they used to expect/hope for …' The full ending shown is '-ūna' (the long 'oo' plus 'na').

5.meaning: A reckoning / an account — the calling-to-account on the Day of Judgment when deeds are tallied and weighed. Here it is the very thing they never expected to face.
5.grammar: A singular masculine verbal noun (pattern fiʿāl) serving as the direct object of 'yarjūna' ('expect/hope for'). The final -an (tanwīn, ـًا) marks it indefinite ('any reckoning') and accusative — the case of the thing acted upon, i.e. what they did not anticipate.
5.root: ح-س-ب (ḥ-s-b) — to count, calculate, reckon, call to account

1.meaning: And they denied, rejected, or called something a lie. The verb describes treating a message or sign as false and refusing to believe it.

parts.en: silent spelling-alif after the plural ending

1.grammar: Past-tense verb. The doubled middle letter (the shadda on the dh) makes it the intensive form: not merely 'denied' but 'denied utterly / flatly rejected'. The -ū ending means the subject is 'they' (a group of males); the final alif is just a spelling convention and is not pronounced. The opening wa- means 'and'.

2.meaning: By Our signs / Our verses. 'Ayat' are signs that point to Allah — both the verses of revelation and the evidences in creation; here joined to 'Our', i.e. belonging to Allah.
2.grammar: A noun phrase, not a verb. The prefix bi- ('with/in') here completes the verb 'denied' — they cried lies 'against / about Our signs'. 'Ayat' is a feminine plural noun. The -i ending is genitive, required because the word follows the preposition bi-. The attached -nā means 'our', so the signs belong to Allah ('the speaker').

3.meaning: A vehement denial / an utter rejection. A verbal noun naming the very act of crying lies, used here to stress how total and emphatic their rejection was.

parts.en: accusative ending ('with… / in the manner of…')

3.grammar: A verbal noun (naming the action of denying), built on an intensive pattern: the doubled dh — written with a shadda, so it is pronounced kidhdhāban (a held, double 'dh'), not kidhāban — conveys doing it repeatedly and emphatically. The -an ending is accusative and works here as an emphasizing object: it underlines the verb — 'they denied Our signs with utter denial'. It does not name a new thing but intensifies the act.
3.root: ك-ذ-ب (k-dh-b) — lying, falsehood

1.meaning: And every / each. Expresses totality — 'each and every one' of whatever follows.
1.grammar: A noun meaning 'every/all', placed before another noun to sweep it up entirely. The -a ending is accusative, marking it as the object of the verb that follows ('We have counted every thing'); it is fronted before its verb for emphasis. The opening wa- means 'and'.

2.meaning: A thing — any single item or matter whatsoever. Paired with 'every' it means absolutely everything that exists.
2.grammar: A singular noun. The -in ending is the genitive case with nunation (the -n sound that marks an indefinite noun, like saying 'a thing'). It is genitive because it follows 'kull' ('every') — literally 'every of a thing', i.e. 'everything'.

3.meaning: We have counted it up / kept full account of it. The verb means to enumerate and comprehend something exhaustively, leaving nothing out — Allah has tallied everything precisely.
3.grammar: Past-tense verb in Form IV (the afʿala pattern, formed by the aleph prefix on the three root letters). This is just the stem pattern that produces aḥṣā, 'to count up / enumerate completely' — it is not a 'doer/agent' marker and does not carry a causative sense here. The -nā ending is the subject 'we' (the royal 'We' of Allah). The final -hu is an attached object pronoun, 'it', referring back to 'every thing'. So: 'We have fully counted it'.
3.root: ح-ص-ي (ḥ-ṣ-y) — to count, enumerate, keep account

4.meaning: As a written record / in a Book. A 'kitab' is something written down; here it means a precise written register in which everything is set down.
4.grammar: A noun. The -an ending is accusative with nunation (indefinite, 'a book'). Here it functions as a circumstantial specifier — explaining how the counting was done: 'We counted it up, [recording it] in writing / as a written record'.

1.meaning: So taste! A command to experience or undergo something directly. Used sternly here: 'taste' the punishment — i.e. suffer and feel it firsthand.

parts.en: silent spelling-alif after the plural ending

1.grammar: A command (imperative) verb. The -ū ending makes it plural and addressed to 'you all' (a group of males) — 'all of you, taste!'. The opening fa- means 'so / then', presenting this as the consequence of what came before. The final alif is silent spelling only.

2.meaning: And never / not at all. A particle that firmly negates a future action — stronger than a plain 'not', it shuts the door on something ever happening.
2.grammar: A negation particle that works only on future verbs and turns them into 'will never'. It also puts the verb that follows into the subjunctive (forcing its ending to -a). It carries no case ending of its own. The fa- prefix links it back to the command ('taste… and We will never…').

3.meaning: We will increase you / add more to you. The verb means to give more of something; here, to add more punishment.

parts.en: we (prefix); doubled by assimilation of the n of 'lan'

3.grammar: A present/future-tense verb. Its prefix na- means the subject is 'we' (the royal 'We' of Allah). The shadda (doubling) on this nūn comes from assimilation: the final nūn of the preceding particle لَنۡ (lan) merges into the nūn of the verb prefix, so لَنۡ + نَزِيد is pronounced lan-nazīd with a single held 'n-n'. Its ending is -a (subjunctive) because 'lan' requires it — together they mean 'We will never increase…'. The attached -kum is the object 'you all' (a group). So: 'We will never give you more (except torment)'.
3.root: ز-ي-د (z-y-d) — to increase, to add

4.meaning: Except / only — a particle of exception that carves out what follows from a preceding negation. After 'they will not taste any coolness or drink,' it introduces the sole grim exception to that statement.
4.grammar: An indeclinable particle of exception (it has no case, tense, or root). It signals that what comes next is excluded from the earlier negation: 'they taste nothing … except ____.' It does not itself change form.

5.meaning: Punishment / torment. Severe suffering inflicted as a penalty; here, the chastisement of the Hereafter.
5.grammar: A noun. The -an ending is accusative with nunation (indefinite). It is the object of 'We will increase you' — specifying what the increase consists of: 'We will only increase you in torment'.

1.meaning: A particle of emphasis placed at the start of a sentence to assert what follows strongly and certainly — roughly 'Indeed…', 'Truly…', 'It is certainly the case that…'. It has no single English word; it stresses the truth of the whole statement.
1.grammar: An emphatic particle that opens a sentence. It puts the noun right after it (here 'the Day of Decision') into the accusative form, and gives the sense 'Indeed/Truly…'. The doubled 'n' (shadda) is intrinsic to the particle; it has no case ending of its own.

2.meaning: For those mindful of Allah / the God-conscious. The 'muttaqin' are people of taqwa — a protective, reverent awareness of Allah that guards them against wrongdoing and moves them to obey Him.

parts.en: one who guards himself / is mindful of Allah

2.grammar: An active participle ('the ones who are God-conscious') turned plural. The li- prefix means 'for / belonging to' and is why the word is genitive. The plural ending is -īna (genitive/accusative form, rather than -ūna), 'those who…'. Together: 'for those mindful of Allah (there is success)'.

3.meaning: A place or attainment of triumph and safety — the salvation, victory, and flourishing the God-conscious win in the Hereafter. It carries both senses: a place of success and the success itself, achieved by being saved from the Fire and granted Paradise.
3.grammar: A noun in the indefinite accusative. The final -an (tanwīn fatḥa) marks the accusative case here because it is the object of the implied verb 'they will have/attain', and the doubled 'n' sound (nunation) signals it is indefinite — 'a triumph/success', not 'the success'. The ma- prefix pattern (mafʿal) typically forms a noun of place or of the action itself.
3.root: ف-و-ز (f-w-z) — to triumph, attain success, be saved

1.meaning: Lush, walled gardens — enclosed orchards thick with trees and fruit. The word specifically denotes gardens girded by a wall or hedge, evoking abundance, beauty, and protected greenery.
1.grammar: A broken (irregular) plural of ḥadīqa ('garden'). The final -a marks the accusative case, here as the object of the implied 'they will have'. It takes a single -a with no nunation (the '-n' sound) because this plural pattern (faʿāʾil, the plural of faʿīla) is 'diptote' — a class of nouns that refuses nunation and uses -a for the accusative.
1.root: ح-د-ق (ḥ-d-q) — to enclose, surround (a garden ringed by a wall)

2.meaning: And grapevines / grapes — clusters of the vine, a prized fruit of the gardens. The plural points to abundant vineyards and their produce.
2.grammar: A connector 'wa' (and) joined to a broken plural of ʿinab ('grape'). The final -an (tanwīn fatḥa) is the accusative case — it continues the list of things the righteous will have — and the doubled 'n' sound marks it as indefinite, 'grapes/vineyards'.

1.meaning: And full-bosomed maidens — youthful female companions of Paradise, described as having rounded, well-developed figures, signifying their fresh and blossoming womanhood.
1.grammar: A connector 'wa' (and) — written with a shadda here because the preceding word ends in a way that doubles it in recitation — joined to a broken plural of kāʿib ('a girl whose bosom is becoming full'). The final -a is the accusative case (still part of the list of what is granted), with no nunation ('-n' sound) because this plural pattern (fawāʿil) is diptote and refuses it.
1.root: ك-ع-ب (k-ʿ-b) — to be rounded/swelling (as a bosom or ankle-bone)

2.meaning: Of equal age, well-matched — companions all of the same youthful age as one another, perfectly suited and equal, with no disparity among them.
2.grammar: A broken plural of tirb ('one of the same age, a peer'), functioning as an adjective describing the maidens of the previous word. The final -an (tanwīn fatḥa) is accusative to agree with the noun it describes, and the doubled 'n' sound marks it indefinite — 'maidens, all peers in age'.
2.root: ت-ر-ب (t-r-b) — to be of the same age / equal (linked to 'turāb', dust — those who played in the same dust as children)

1.meaning: And a cup — a drinking vessel, here understood as a cup of pure, delightful wine. By idiom 'kaʾs' denotes specifically a cup filled with drink, not an empty one.
1.grammar: A connector 'wa' (and) — doubled (shadda) in recitation after the preceding word — joined to the noun kaʾs. The final -an (tanwīn fatḥa) is the accusative, continuing the list of gifts, and the doubled 'n' sound shows it is indefinite, 'a cup'.
1.root: ك-أ-س (k-ʾ-s) — a cup filled with drink

2.meaning: Brimming, filled to the top — describing the cup as full and overflowing, an image of generous, unstinting abundance.
2.grammar: An adjective describing the 'cup' of the previous word. The final -an (tanwīn fatḥa) is accusative to match the noun it qualifies, and the doubled 'n' sound marks it indefinite — 'a brimming cup'.
2.root: د-ه-ق (d-h-q) — to fill up completely, make brim over

1.meaning: Not — a particle of negation. Placed before a present-tense verb, it denies the action: 'they do not / will not...'. Here it negates their tasting of any relief.
1.grammar: A negating particle. It carries no case ending of its own; it simply turns the following present-tense verb negative. With a present-tense verb describing the future, it means 'they will not...'.

2.meaning: They hear / they will hear — to perceive sound with the ears. In context it states what the people of Paradise will NOT hear: no idle or false speech.
2.grammar: A present/future-tense verb, 3rd person masculine plural: 'they hear / will hear'. The ya- prefix marks the 3rd person masculine but does not by itself distinguish singular from plural; it is the ya-…-ūna circumfix together that encodes 3rd-person masculine plural. The -ūna ending makes it plural ('they', many men) and marks the indicative mood — a plain factual statement (as opposed to a command or a negated/subjunctive form, which would drop the final -na, giving -ū).
2.root: س-م-ع (s-m-ʿ) — to hear, listen, perceive by ear

3.meaning: In it / therein — the preposition 'in' fused with 'it,' referring back to Hell (feminine). It locates the abiding: they remain inside it.
3.grammar: Preposition 'fī' ('in') with the attached pronoun '-hā' ('it,' feminine), pointing back to Jahannam. Attached pronouns do not change for case; together they mean 'in it / therein.' (The long final vowel is stretched in recitation.)
3.root: — (preposition + pronoun; no triliteral root)

4.meaning: Idle, vain talk — empty, frivolous, or meaningless speech that has no benefit or worth. It denotes the worthless chatter that is entirely absent from Paradise.
4.grammar: A verbal noun in the indefinite accusative. The final -an (tanwīn fatḥa) marks it as the object of 'they will not hear', and the doubled 'n' sound marks it indefinite — 'any idle talk'.
4.root: ل-غ-و (l-gh-w) — to speak idly/vainly, utter what is worthless

5.meaning: A linking 'and not' — it joins 'coolness' to the next item ('drink') while extending the negation over it, so the sense is 'neither coolness nor any drink.'
5.grammar: Two particles with no case or tense of their own. 'wa' is the conjunction 'and'; 'lā' is the particle of negation that carries the earlier 'they will not taste' onto the following noun. (The 'w' is written doubled/with shadda because the preceding word's ending assimilates into it in recitation.) Together they mean 'and not …', i.e. 'nor.'

6.meaning: Lying, falsehood — the giving of the lie, false or denying speech. Paired with 'idle talk', it completes the picture: in Paradise there is neither empty chatter nor any lie.
6.grammar: A verbal noun (intensive fiʿʿāl pattern, with a doubled middle consonant — hence the geminated dhdh) in the indefinite accusative — a second object of 'they will not hear'. The final -an (tanwīn fatḥa) is accusative and the doubled 'n' sound marks it indefinite, 'any falsehood'.
6.root: ك-ذ-ب (k-dh-b) — to lie, give the lie, deny falsely

1.meaning: A recompense — a repayment or requital, the due return given for one's deeds. Here it frames the punishment just described as exactly what their actions earned.
1.grammar: A singular masculine verbal noun in the accusative. The accusative here gives the sense 'as a recompense' (an adverbial/causative accusative explaining why or in what capacity the punishment is given). The final -an (tanwīn, written ـً after the hamza) marks it indefinite and accusative.

2.meaning: From — a particle marking origin or starting-point, showing where something comes from or proceeds out of. Here it points to the source of the reward: 'from your Lord'.
2.grammar: A preposition (a small linking word) meaning 'from'. It has no case ending of its own; instead it puts the noun after it ('your Lord') into the genitive case. Its sukūn (the small mark over the final 'n') simply shows the 'n' is unvoweled and the word is complete.

3.meaning: Your Lord — Allah as the Sustainer, Master, and Nurturer who creates, owns, provides for, and governs all things and brings them to their completion. 'Rabb' bundles lordship, ownership, and tender upbringing into one term; the attached 'your' addresses the Prophet (and by extension the listener).
3.grammar: A noun ('Lord') with an attached possessive pronoun -ka ('your', addressing one male). The -i ending on rabb is the genitive case, required because the preposition 'min' ('from') precedes it — 'from your Lord'. The -ka pronoun both shows possession ('your Lord') and is itself in the genitive position as the thing possessed.
3.root: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — to nurture, sustain, master, bring to completion

4.meaning: A gift or bestowal — something given freely and graciously, without the recipient having any claim to it. Here it describes the reward of the righteous as a pure, generous grant flowing from the Lord's bounty.
4.grammar: A masculine verbal noun in the indefinite accusative case. The doubled '-an' (tanwīn fatḥ) marks it as indefinite ('a gift, some gift') and as accusative — here functioning as a specifying/explanatory object describing the manner of the reward: it is given 'as a gift'.
4.root: ع-ط-و / ع-ط-ي (ʿ-ṭ-w / ʿ-ṭ-y) — to give, to bestow, to hand over. The root is weak in its final letter; classical lexicons list both forms, and the Form I imperfect يُعْطِي (yuʿṭī) reflects the ع-ط-ي variant.

5.meaning: A reckoning / an account — the calling-to-account on the Day of Judgment when deeds are tallied and weighed. Here it is the very thing they never expected to face.
5.grammar: A singular masculine verbal noun (pattern fiʿāl) serving as the direct object of 'yarjūna' ('expect/hope for'). The final -an (tanwīn, ـًا) marks it indefinite ('any reckoning') and accusative — the case of the thing acted upon, i.e. what they did not anticipate.
5.root: ح-س-ب (ḥ-s-b) — to count, calculate, reckon, call to account

1.meaning: Lord, Master, and Sustainer — the One who owns, nurtures, and brings to perfection. 'Rabb' is far richer than 'master': it combines ownership, loving cultivation, governance, and continuous care of all that He has made.
1.grammar: A masculine noun in the genitive case. The '-i' ending is genitive: it links this word to what follows in a possessive chain — 'Lord OF the heavens and the earth'. (Following Qur'anic recitation the doubled 'r' carries assimilation from a preceding word.)
1.root: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — to nurture, sustain, master, bring up

2.meaning: The heavens — the skies and all the celestial realms above, encompassing everything raised high over the earth.
2.grammar: A feminine plural noun, definite ('the heavens'), in the genitive case. The genitive shows on the sound feminine plural as '-i' (replacing the usual '-u'); it appears here because the word is the possessed second term of 'Lord of the heavens'. The 'l-' of 'al-' assimilates into the 's' (a 'sun letter'), heard as 'as-'.
2.root: س-م-و (s-m-w) — to be high, to rise; that which is elevated above

3.meaning: And the earth — the ground and the world beneath, paired with the heavens to express the whole of creation.
3.grammar: A feminine noun, definite ('the earth'), joined by the prefix 'wa-' ('and') and in the genitive case. The '-i' ending is genitive because it is coupled to 'the heavens' within the possessive phrase 'Lord of the heavens and the earth'.
3.root: أَرْض (arḍ) is a primitive noun (ism jāmid) — it is not derived from a verbal triliteral root. The consonants أ-ر-ض are simply those of the noun itself; classical lexicographers record no confirmed verbal root from which it springs.

4.meaning: And whatever — 'and that which', referring here to all things that lie in between. 'Mā' is a connective word meaning 'what / whatever / that which', used for non-human or unspecified things.
4.grammar: A connective relative word ('that which / whatever') introduced by 'wa-' ('and'). It does not inflect for case — its form is fixed. Grammatically it stands alongside 'the heavens and the earth' as a further thing that the Lord owns: '…and whatever is between them'.

5.meaning: Between the two of them — in the space separating the heavens and the earth; everything occupying that interval.
5.grammar: An adverb of place, 'bayna' ('between'), fixed with an '-a' ending, joined to the attached dual pronoun 'humā' ('the two of them'). The pronoun is in the genitive/possessive position after the adverb, and its dual form specifically means 'both', i.e. the heavens and the earth.
5.root: ب-ي-ن (b-y-n) — to be distinct, to separate; the space between

6.meaning: The Most Gracious, the All-Merciful — a divine name of Allah denoting His vast, all-embracing mercy that overflows to every creature. 'Ar-Raḥmān' expresses an intense, encompassing compassion that is uniquely His.
6.grammar: A definite name in the genitive case. The '-i' ending is genitive: here it stands as a further description of 'your Lord' (in apposition to the genitive 'Lord'), 'the Lord… the Most Gracious'. The 'l-' of 'al-' assimilates into the 'r' (a 'sun letter'), pronounced 'ar-'. The intensive form (faʿlān) conveys fullness and abundance of mercy.

7.meaning: Not — a particle of negation. Placed before a present-tense verb, it denies the action: 'they do not / will not...'. Here it negates their tasting of any relief.
7.grammar: A negating particle. It carries no case ending of its own; it simply turns the following present-tense verb negative. With a present-tense verb describing the future, it means 'they will not...'.

8.meaning: They possess / they have power — to own or have authority and control over something. Here, with the negation in the verse, it means they have no power or authority to do so.
8.grammar: A present/future-tense verb, third person masculine plural: 'they own / have power'. The 'ya-…-ūna' frame marks 'they' (masculine plural) acting now or in the future. The final '-na' is the indicative ending (the verb is not negated grammatically by a particle here, so it keeps its full '-ūna' form). In context it is governed by the preceding negation 'lā', giving 'they do not possess'.
8.root: م-ل-ك (m-l-k) — to own, to possess, to have dominion

9.meaning: From Him — proceeding or coming from Him (the Most Gracious). It marks origin or source: any speaking 'from Him' / in His presence.
9.grammar: The preposition 'min' ('from') with the attached third person masculine singular pronoun '-hu' ('Him'). The pronoun sits in the genitive/object position after the preposition. The vowel is 'min-hu' (the 'h' keeps its 'u' here), meaning 'from Him'.
9.root: — (min is a preposition; no triliteral root)

10.meaning: Speech directed at someone, an address — to speak to, converse with, or petition another. Here it is the act of addressing the Lord: none will have the power to speak to Him or plead with Him except by His leave.
10.grammar: A masculine verbal noun in the indefinite accusative case. The '-an' (tanwīn fatḥ) marks it as indefinite ('any address, any speaking') and accusative — it is the direct object of 'they have power over': '…they will not have power over any addressing of Him'.
10.root: خ-ط-ب (kh-ṭ-b) — to address, to speak to, to discourse

1.meaning: The Day — here the great appointed Day, identified in the next word as the Day of Decision/Judgment.
1.grammar: A masculine noun, 'day'. The '-a' ending is accusative; it appears because this noun is the subject that the emphatic particle 'inna' (id 44) governs — 'inna' forces the following noun into this '-a' form. It is also the first part of the phrase 'the Day OF Decision', completed by the next word.

2.meaning: He/it stands, will stand — to rise to one's feet and take one's station. Here it describes the spirit and the angels rising and standing up (in ranks) on that Day.
2.grammar: A present/future-tense verb, third person masculine singular: 'he/it stands' or 'will stand'. The 'ya-' prefix marks the 'he/it' subject acting now or in the future. The final '-u' is the indicative ending, showing the verb is in its plain, uninterrupted statement form (not commanded or negated by a jussive/subjunctive particle).
2.root: ق-و-م (q-w-m) — to stand, to rise, to take up a station

3.meaning: The Spirit — a noble, exalted being. In this context it is widely understood as the angel Jibrīl (Gabriel) or a great spirit/angel who will stand on the Day of Judgement; the word's root sense is 'spirit, breath of life'.
3.grammar: A definite noun in the nominative case. The '-u' ending is nominative, marking it as the subject — the one who performs the standing: 'the Spirit will stand'. The 'l-' of 'al-' assimilates into the 'r' (a 'sun letter'), pronounced 'ar-rūḥ'.
3.root: ر-و-ح (r-w-ḥ) — spirit, breath, life; rest and ease

4.meaning: and the Angels — the noble created beings of light who serve Allah and carry out His commands; here pictured standing in ranks on the Day of Judgement.
4.grammar: A plural noun with the connector 'wa' (and) and the definite article 'al-' (the). The final '-u' is the nominative ending, marking 'the angels' as the subject — the ones who will stand in ranks. The plural pattern (malāʾikah) is a broken plural of 'malak' (an angel).
4.root: ء-ل-ك (ʾ-l-k) — to send on a mission/errand; an angel is a messenger/envoy of Allah. (The base verb is alaka, 'to send,' so the root letters are hamza–lām–kāf.)

5.meaning: in rows / ranks — drawn up in orderly lines, the way disciplined troops or worshippers stand shoulder to shoulder.
5.grammar: A noun in the accusative with the '-an' ending (tanwīn, the doubled 'n' sound 'an'). Here it functions adverbially, describing the manner of standing: 'standing (in) rows.' The accusative is what gives it the sense 'in a state of being ranked.'
5.root: ص-ف-ف (ṣ-f-f) — to line up, arrange in a row.

6.meaning: not — a particle that negates the verb after it. With a present-tense verb it denies the action: 'they do not / will not speak.'
6.grammar: A negation particle placed before a present-tense verb to negate it. It does not change the verb's ending; it simply turns 'they speak' into 'they do not speak.' (The doubled 'll' in the transliteration reflects how the preceding word runs into it in recitation.)

7.meaning: they speak / they will speak — to talk, to utter words, expressed with emphasis on a full, deliberate act of speaking.
7.grammar: A present/future-tense verb, 3rd-person masculine plural. The 'ya-' prefix marks the present tense, and the '-ūna' ending means 'they (men)' and shows the verb is in its plain indicative form (a complete statement). With 'lā' before it, the whole phrase means 'they will not speak.' The stem (Form V, takallama) carries the sense of deliberately engaging in speech.

8.meaning: Except / only — a particle of exception that carves out what follows from a preceding negation. After 'they will not taste any coolness or drink,' it introduces the sole grim exception to that statement.
8.grammar: An indeclinable particle of exception (it has no case, tense, or root). It signals that what comes next is excluded from the earlier negation: 'they taste nothing … except ____.' It does not itself change form.

9.meaning: whoever / the one who — a relative word standing for an unnamed person: 'the one whom…' Here it picks out the only ones permitted to speak.
9.grammar: A relative pronoun used for people ('who, whoever, the one who'). It is invariable — its form never changes for case. In this verse it follows the exception particle 'illā' and is the subject of its clause: the one who received permission is the one who acts ('except the one whom the Most Gracious has permitted'). The beneficiary 'to him' is carried separately by 'lahu.'

10.meaning: he permitted / gave leave — to grant permission or authorization for something to be done.
10.grammar: A past-tense verb, 3rd-person masculine singular ('he permitted'). The final '-a' is the standard past-tense ending for 'he,' marking a completed act. Though past in form, in this context it carries a timeless/future sense: 'the one whom He permits.'
10.root: ء-ذ-ن (ʾ-dh-n) — permission, to give leave; also linked to 'ear'/listening.

11.meaning: for him / to him — i.e., permission is granted in his favour.
11.grammar: A preposition 'li-' (to/for) joined to the attached pronoun '-hu' (him). The base preposition's vowel shifts to 'la-' before this pronoun. Together: 'for him,' completing 'has given leave to him.' The '-u' vowel on '-hu' is its natural form here after the 'a' sound.

12.meaning: the Most Gracious / All-Merciful — a name of Allah denoting His vast, all-encompassing mercy and compassion extended to all creation.
12.grammar: A name of Allah formed with the article 'al-' (the). The final '-u' is the nominative ending, marking it as the subject — the One who grants permission: 'whom the Most Gracious has permitted.' The pattern (faʿlān) conveys intensity and fullness of mercy. ('al-' assimilates into the following 'r,' heard as 'ar-raḥmān.')

13.meaning: and he said / and he will say — to speak or utter; with the connector 'and' linking it to the preceding clause.
13.grammar: The connector 'wa' (and) plus a past-tense verb, 3rd-person masculine singular ('he said'). The final '-a' is the 'he' past-tense ending marking a completed act. In this verse it carries a future/conditional sense alongside 'adhina': 'and (who) says what is right.'
